transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. It's really nice to meet you too. 

Um, I guess I'm here because I've been having just a little bit of trouble at work lately. I work in meat processing, and... well, it's kind of embarrassing to admit, but I keep messing up my routines. Not the whole thing, I promise! I'm usually really good at starting things. But I'll start the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then somehow I just... I leave out the very last parts. 

I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, and I really do try my absolute best to get it all done perfectly. I just keep missing the end of the instructions. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you the kind of information you need.
Before you finish those tasks, do you get unwanted thoughts that something isn’t right and feel driven to check or repeat things?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I'm sorry if that's not what you were looking for, but I don't really get thoughts like that. It's never really a feeling that something is wrong or that I need to go back and check it again. I just... kind of lose my place, I guess? Or my mind just wanders off to something else before I finish the very end of the task. 

I really hope I'm explaining that okay? Does that make sense for what you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Did you have the same kind of trouble with finishing tasks or staying focused when you were a child?

Um, well... yes, I think so. I mean, I don't want it to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I was actually pretty smart, I promise. My mom even kept some of my old report cards from around fourth grade, and they always said I was really bright. 

But... well, they also said I needed a lot of reminders to finish my classwork and actually turn in my homework. I always understood what we were learning, I really did. I just... I guess I would miss chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was right there next to me to keep me on track. It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or ignore them, I just sort of drifted. 

Does that help? I hope that's the kind of thing you were wondering about. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Growing up, did you often have trouble understanding social cues, like knowing when someone was joking or getting bored with what you were saying?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I had trouble with that. I mean, I really hope I didn't! I've always tried my best to be polite and pay attention to how other people are feeling. 

I can usually tell right away if someone is joking around. And... well, I actually worry a lot about whether I'm boring people or talking too much, so I'm always looking out for that. If someone seems uninterested or quiet, I definitely notice it because I never want to be a bother to anyone. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were expecting, I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest so you have exactly what you need to figure this out. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Do you also have this same problem finishing things at home?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes struggle a little bit at home, too. But I really try my best to keep on top of things! I mean, my apartment isn't a disaster or anything, I promise. 

It's just... well, like with laundry, for example. I'll get it washed and dried, no problem. But then... maybe the basket sits in my room for a few days before I actually put everything away? Or I'll start doing the dishes, but then I'll remember I need to wipe down the counters, and then I get sidetracked organizing a drawer... and then the dishes are just sitting there in the soapy water. 

I always mean to finish everything, I really do. It just sort of gets away from me sometimes. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to make sure I'm giving you a good picture of how things are.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Um, worrying? Oh, no, I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, I definitely don't sit around worrying about nothing! I try really hard to stay positive and, you know, take things as they come. 

I guess sometimes I might get a little stressed, like anyone would, especially if work is busy or I feel like I'm falling behind on things. But I don't think I worry about random things for no reason. I really try not to be one of those people who complains or gets worked up over every little thing. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I can try to think of an example if you need one, but I honestly don't think I'm a big worrier. I just want to make sure I'm answering this right for you.
